classification.difficultyReason: Requires translating two random cut positions into a two-dimensional region and calculating a complementary probability.

content.prompt:
A piece of string of length 2 metres is cut at two random points chosen independently and uniformly. Find the probability that one of the three resulting pieces is at least 1 metre long.

Hint: It may be easier to find the probability that all three pieces are less than 1 metre.

answer.short:
$\frac34$.

Represent the two cut positions in a square and subtract the region where all three pieces are shorter than 1 metre.
answer.worked:
Let $x$ and $y$ be the cut positions measured in metres from one end. The pair $(x,y)$ is uniformly distributed over the square $[0,2]\times[0,2]$, of area $4$.

When $x<y$, the three lengths are $x$, $y-x$ and $2-y$. All three are less than 1 precisely when
$$x<1,\qquad y-x<1,\qquad y>1.$$
These conditions describe the triangle with vertices $(0,1)$, $(1,1)$ and $(1,2)$, excluding its boundary. Its area is $\frac12$. The case $y<x$ gives a reflected triangle of the same area. Boundaries have probability zero.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{all pieces}<1\text{ m})&=\frac{2\times\frac12}{4}\\P(\text{all pieces}<1\text{ m})&=\frac14\\P(\text{at least one piece}\ge1\text{ m})&=1-\frac14\\P(\text{at least one piece}\ge1\text{ m})&=\frac34.\end{align*}$$
